witb_placement_inference.description: What's-in-the-Box: infer which of two boxes holds each listed household object from parsed object descriptions, box measurements and per-box sound-classifier posteriors. Scored on 800 hidden scenarios (2,841 object queries) against the objects' true placements. This replaces the paper's correlation with 54 participants' mean ratings on 20 videos, which were never released (see _paper_reported).

truth_correlation.description: Pearson correlation, over every (object, box) query, between the predicted probability that the object is in that box and whether it actually is. Same statistic the paper uses (Figure 3: correlation over object-in-box ratings), with true placements as the target.

brier_score.description: Mean over objects of half the squared error between the predicted box distribution and the true box (proper scoring rule; penalises both poor discrimination and miscalibration).

log_loss.description: Mean negative log probability assigned to each object's true box, with probabilities floored at 1e-4 (proper scoring rule; penalises confident mistakes).

_paper_reported.note: Paper (arXiv 2506.14212, Figure 3): Pearson r between model ratings and mean human ratings over 20 stimuli (2-5 objects, 2 boxes, 54 participants). The gym's target is the true placement on synthetic hidden scenarios, so these numbers are not on the gym's scale and are not matched.
